capabilities.name: Persistent Thread chat
capabilities.purpose: Save a multi-turn assistant conversation with branches, drafts, refs and kept results.
capabilities.status_reason: Thread CRUD, persistence and streaming orchestration are implemented and assertion-backed; provider and owner use were not observed.
model_requirements: configured admitted model route for assistant turns
capabilities.trust_boundary: Owner thread input is persisted and frozen before an admitted model child; kept output is a separate local write.
capabilities.egress: The frozen model route determines whether prompt material leaves the hub.
capabilities.authority: Authenticated owner thread operation and frozen route plan; tool effects use the separate tool gate.

sources.claim: ThreadService owns thread CRUD and turn orchestration.
The repository persists threads, messages, refs, drafts and tool policy.
The HTTP router serves concrete Thread routes.

tests.assertion: Creating a thread returns 201 and a durable th_ id.
Import is repeatable and returns the same result on replay.

limitations: No model call, live stream or owner walk was run.
Published releases may expose fewer features.

capabilities.name: Persistent Thread tool loop
capabilities.purpose: Offer a bounded MCP tool palette inside a Thread turn and retain tool results and receipts.
capabilities.status_reason: The pass loop, tool classification, deadlines, sensitive result marking and held decisions are implemented; no provider loop was run.
model_requirements: assistant route that can emit tool calls
network_requirements: tool/provider boundary when a tool egresses
capabilities.trust_boundary: Each offered tool is classified and admitted as a child; an effect proposal can wait for a named owner decision.
capabilities.egress: Tool-specific providers and effect connectors may cross egress after the tool gate admits them.
capabilities.authority: Control-mode matrix, thread policy and owner decision handle determine admission; tool names do not grant rights.

sources.claim: The executor owns tool admission, decision, execution and cancellation states.
The closed policy table maps policy, control mode and tool class to admit/hold/deny.
A turn persists input and starts the bounded streaming/tool loop.

tests.assertion: The test asserts started, pending, result, delta and done frame order with a succeeded tool result.
The tenth-pass cap closes the turn with pass_cap_reached.
A denied held call emits tool_denied and does not execute the effect.

limitations: No live external tool or provider call was made.
Tool palette is mode-specific and intentionally bounded.

capabilities.name: Interview conversation
capabilities.purpose: Use one owner-only Thread mode to record sourced facts and reviewable suggestions.
capabilities.status_reason: The revisioned Interview reducer, section palette, exact quote provenance and MCP tools are source-present and assertion-backed.
capabilities.trust_boundary: Interview state is owner-authored context; suggestions remain proposals and never install automation or confer authority.
capabilities.egress: An Interview model turn may use its selected route; recorded facts are local until another explicit capability reads them.
capabilities.authority: InterviewService.require_owner and expected revision; People content requires a protected handoff.

sources.claim: The seeded Interview mode defines eight sections and bounded tool palettes.
InterviewService owns durable context and replay-safe commands.
The MCP family requires owner authority and dispatches structured Interview commands.

tests.assertion: Same command identity replays, while a conflicting command is refused atomically.
Protected People handoff refuses before the turn is persisted.
The conversation test checks tool calls, receipts, saved suggestion, Keep and revisiting state.

limitations: No owner Interview sitting was observed.
Unsupported integrations and general delegation remain ideas/manual recipes.

capabilities.trust_boundary: MCP schemas describe callable operations; principal authentication and service policy decide whether a call can run.

The catalogue contains closed tool schemas and service dispatch names.

capabilities.egress: Hydrated blocks may be passed to a selected model by their caller; hydration alone does not send them.
capabilities.authority: Caller principal read authority and explicit refs/query; no evidence read grants effect authority.

sources.claim: The shared resolver returns bounded blocks and hydration statistics.

tests.assertion: Phase, evidence and roadmap refs hydrate the expected block kinds.
An unknown story returns no block and a named unknown ref.

limitations: No live source hydration or model call was run.
The resolver does not prove semantic truth of source text.

The router exposes CRUD, run and cancel routes.

tests.assertion: Branching control flow is refused by linearization.

capabilities.name: Coder Gate held tool call
capabilities.purpose: Hold a matched risky Coder tool call for owner decision with bounded previews, idempotency and fail-closed recovery.
capabilities.status_reason: Agent hook, hub state machine, bounded previews, expiry and restart invalidation are implemented and assertion-backed; no armed hook was run here.
inputs: argument hash and potentially sensitive prefix
capabilities.trust_boundary: SHA-256 plus a 120-character canonical JSON prefix reaches the hub. This is truncation, not secret removal: short inputs and prefix secrets can be retained. Held approval requests are invalidated at restart.
capabilities.egress: Gate controls whether the Coder process may perform its own tool egress; the Gate hook itself sends a bounded but potentially sensitive argument prefix to the hub.
capabilities.authority: Double opt-in matcher, authenticated agent principal and owner decision; expiry, outage and restart deny.

sources.claim: The hook has inert, bounded-preview, idempotent and fail-closed paths.
The repository owns legal transitions, idempotent arrivals and audit rows.
The hub serves proposal, decision, receipt and audit routes.

tests.assertion: Unarmed matching does not contact the hub or create a proposal.
An armed unreachable hub produces a named deny.
An idempotency-key argument swap refuses and invalidates the original hold.
The registered Gate claim confirms a short synthetic credential-like marker survives in the canonical JSON prefix; it disproves secret-removal semantics.

limitations: No gate was armed, no agent credential issued and no real Coder call was held.
The default matcher covers Bash only.
